title: Cast removal
what: The cast is cut with a special saw or scissors and removed. Then the doctor checks how the bone has healed.
why: When the time your doctor set is over, or the cast needs to be replaced.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; a follow-up X-ray and exam the same day
tell_doctor: If it hurt, burned, or smelled under the cast
If your fingers or toes went numb

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Bring loose clothes and shoes. The arm or leg may be a little swollen.

steps: Usually a follow-up X-ray is done first
The cast is cut with a saw that vibrates, rather than spins
The cast is opened and removed
The padding and sleeve are cut with scissors
The doctor checks your skin and movement
The doctor explains what you can and cannot do next
feel: Noise, vibration, and warmth from the saw. The saw does not cut skin
The arm or leg feels light and weak
The joint is stiff, and moving is hard
after: The skin is dry and flaky. Wash it with warm water and use cream
Swelling may last a few days
Muscles recover gradually. Do exercises as your doctor says
red_flags: Strong swelling, pain, and redness in the calf: see a doctor right away
Sudden pain or a change in shape after removal

faq.a: No. It vibrates and cuts only the hard cast, not soft skin. It may feel warm.

faq.q: Why is my arm so weak?
faq.a: The muscles got weaker without movement. Strength returns over a few weeks of exercise.

reminders.text: Your cast comes off tomorrow. Bring past X-rays, loose clothes, and comfortable shoes.
